sections.title: Course Logistics and Overview
sections.description: Professor Jelani Nelson introduces the course staff, grading policy, scribing requirements, and final project expectations.

sections.title: The Predecessor Problem
sections.description: The lecture defines the static and dynamic predecessor problems and explains how they relate to the limits of comparison-based sorting.

sections.title: vEB and Fusion Tree Comparison
sections.description: A high-level overview of Van Emde Boas trees and Fusion trees is provided, comparing their performance across different word sizes.

sections.title: The Word RAM Model
sections.description: The instructor defines the Word RAM model and the specific constant-time bitwise and arithmetic operations available for algorithm design.

sections.title: vEB Recursive Structure
sections.description: The internal fields of a Van Emde Boas tree are defined, including clusters, summaries, and the recursive partitioning of the universe.

sections.title: vEB Query and Insertion Logic
sections.description: The lecture details the pseudocode for predecessor queries and insertions, emphasizing the one-call recursion strategy to maintain efficiency.

sections.title: Space Optimization via Hashing
sections.description: Discussion on reducing the space complexity of Van Emde Boas trees from the universe size to linear space using hash-based dictionaries.

sections.title: Dictionary Problems and X-fast Tries
sections.description: An exploration of the dictionary problem leads into the construction of X-fast tries using bit arrays and binary trees.

sections.title: Searching X-fast Tries
sections.description: The instructor explains how to perform binary searches on tree levels and use bit-shifting to access ancestors in constant time.

sections.title: Y-fast Tries and Indirection
sections.description: The lecture concludes with the implementation of Y-fast tries using indirection to achieve optimal linear space and amortized update times.
